newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TNT bid unconditional from 50 pct - KPN.
newsitem.headline: TNT bid unconditional from 50 pct - KPN.

text.p: Dutch postal and telecommunications group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said on Friday that its takeover bid for TNT would be declared unconditional if its stake rises above 50 percent and includes the 105 million shares owned by Bankers Trust.
KPN said it now owned 33.3 percent of TNT's ordinary shares and 25.0 percent of TNT's converting preference shares.
KPN previously said the bid would be unconditional from a level of 90 percent of acceptances.

"KPN announces that, if it receives sufficient acceptances to its ordinary offer to increase its entitlement to greater than 50 percent of the ordinary shares of TNT on issue as at the date of KPN's offers, including at least 105 million ordinary shares from interests associated with Bankers Trust, it will promptly declare both its ordinary and converting preference share offers free of all conditions, including the 90 per cent acceptance conditions," KPN said.
KPN said on Monday it had extended the closing date on its A$2.0 billion bid for TNT Ltd by nine days to December 12.
The bid of A$2.45 per share has been recommended by TNT directors.
TNT's shares closed up one cent at A$2.41 on Thursday.
BT held 19.99 percent of TNT shares.
